**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

**Title (English, from literature):** Matchmaking

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The fifth rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* class in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* is titled *Sañcaritta* ("Matchmaking"). The text details the disciplinary rule and case-law analysis concerning a Buddhist monastic who acts as an intermediary or go-between to arrange a relationship between a man and a woman, an infraction punishable by formal suspension (*saṅghādisesa*). The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In agreement with these records, computational analysis by DharmaNexus registers extensive cross-language alignments with Tibetan versions of the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003) and *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon and commentarial literature, DharmaNexus detects widespread formulaic reuse between this text and other disciplinary rules (including *Saṅghādisesa* 1 and several *Pārājika* rules), the *Parivāra*, the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, and later treatises and sub-commentaries such as the *Khuddasikkhā-mūlasikkhā*, *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā*, and *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
